extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, and copyholders involved in book and journal production
extracted.subtask_description: Practical production rules and behavioural standards for preparing manuscripts, marking and returning proofs, and performing proofreading and copyholding in scholarly or book publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be either typewritten or in a perfectly clear handwriting (typewritten preferable). Sheets should be of uniform size (q?xii" desirable), use only one side of the paper, never be rolled (place flat in a box or envelope), and not be fastened together except by pins or clips which can be easily removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When fastening one piece of a page to another use mucilage, not pins (pins liable to become unfastened and slips lost). Liberal margins should be left at the top and left-hand side for reader/printer directions. Pages should be numbered consecutively; inserted and omitted pages should be clearly indicated (e.g., insert after p. 4 mark '4A','4B'; omitted pages indicate by numbering p. 4, '4-7'). Additions to original pages should be placed after the sheets to which they belong and marked 'Insert A', 'Insert B'; mark insertion points ('Here insert A') on margins of originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs should be plainly indicated either by indenting the first line or by a ^ mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote form and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes should be clearly designated and separated from the text (e.g., by running a line across the page or by using ink of different color). The word in the text carrying the note should be followed by a superior figure corresponding to that preceding the note; footnotes should never be run into the text in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some writers fold the paper using two-thirds for text and one-third for notes. Number footnotes consecutively throughout an article or by chapters in a book (recommended because in matter set on the linotype machine the slightest change necessitates resetting the whole line; numbering anew on each page is impracticable). Note: monotype or hand-setting do not face the same resetting difficulty—changing a number there simply substitutes one figure for another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of preliminary and supporting copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Copy for title-pages, prefaces, tables of contents, etc., should be submitted with the manuscript; copy for indices should be compiled from the special set of page-proofs furnished for that purpose and promptly delivered to the printers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnecessary delay is often caused by postponing these details until the last minute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading and returning proofs promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and return your proofs promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In marking proof-sheets, use the standard proofreaders' marks; do not adopt a system of your own. Be careful to answer all queries in the proofs. Remember that changes in the type cost money and that omission or addition of words may necessitate resetting and repaging; make your manuscript as perfect as possible before delivering it to the printer. Necessary alterations should be made in the galley-proof. Corrections in plates should be studiously avoided as they are expensive and apt to injure the plates. The original manuscript should be returned with the galley-proof so the proofreader may refer to it; each successive set of proofs returned should be accompanied by the previous marked set to assist in calculating cost of alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader professional responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Read everything as if you yourself were the author, and take responsibility for accuracy; be particularly careful about proper names and figures and, if copy is not perfectly clear, look it up or query the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make queries clear (a simple query often not enough). Be discreet—avoid foolish questions. Recognize room for differences of opinion in grammar and logic; grant writers privilege of preferring their forms. Study the 'personal equation' of editors and others with whom you work. Never hesitate to correct anything palpably wrong; you will be held responsible for errors that pass under your watch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise independent judgment on style
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ask authors or editors to decide questions of style; the Manual of Style is primarily meant for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn its rules by heart so you may correct any violation without asking questions. Stand on your own feet; if copy is not prepared, you ought to be capable of preparing it yourself. Do not excuse yourself with 'I thought the copy was edited' or that 'the author knew what he wanted.' Editors and authors are fallible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader workflow, time management, and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate speed but prioritize accuracy; notify the person in charge if work is accumulating or you cannot meet promised deadlines; in unavoidable 'rush' cases, protect yourself by stating you did your best in the time allotted but disclaim further responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If memoranda or verbal instructions bearing on a piece of work are given, you are expected to see they are adhered to. Whoever has the final revision for press should ensure all preliminary matter (title, copyright, contents) is complete. Contents of journals should be made up when the first page-proofs are read. Put your initial at the top of every galley you read or revise to save time tracing proofs and to ensure credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyholder duties and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate a low, soft, clear reading voice; ensure small words are audibly read as they are as essential as big ones; enunciate plural -s distinctly; regulate and equalize your speed; do not guess at words—look closely and consider context; sit at right angles to your reader so you can watch the hand; give reader time to make corrections (slow up when pencil is put to paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evolve your own system of signals (e.g., tap pencil once for each italicized word) so as not to waste time by saying 'in italics' each time. Do not waste time over matters of style—the proofreader is supposed to know the rules. Be careful in transferring marks (a mark in the wrong place can produce two errors). Arrange copy and proof-sheets neatly and consecutively when sending out proofs; consult the job ticket for number and address (send two if no number; send to editor if no address). Unless otherwise directed, send out proofs as soon as an article is completed. Manuscript should accompany galley-proof; foul proof (author's marked galley-proof) should accompany page-proof. Indicate contents of envelopes in lower left-hand corner. Fasten pins in the center at the top, not diagonally. Return volumes to the file each evening. Act as housekeeper of the proof-room—keep records and files so everything can be located promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard proofreaders' marks
rubrics_metrics.description: In marking proofs use the standard proofreaders' marks rather than inventing your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: put in capitals; put in small capitals; put in lower case; put in roman type; put in italics; put in bold face type; delete (take X out); letter reversed (turn); indent / make new paragraph; put in space; close up (no space); adjust spacing; wrong font or character of wrong size or style; transpose; carry left or right; elevate; depress; correct imperfect letter; shove down where space shows between words; straighten crooked line; restore or retain words crossed out; print as logotype; indicate words omitted; (T) = query to author ('Is this right?').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary plate corrections and be cost-conscious
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections in plates should be studiously avoided because they are expensive and apt to injure the plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that changes in type cost money; the omission or addition of a word in the middle of a paragraph may necessitate resetting from that point on and may involve repaging the entire article or chapter. Make manuscripts as perfect as possible and confine alterations to galley-proofs whenever feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering and linotype/monotype considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Because matter set on the linotype machine requires resetting of whole lines for the slightest change, numbering of footnotes is best done consecutively throughout an article or by chapters in a book rather than restarting numbering on each page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This difficulty is not met with in matter set on the monotype machine or by hand, where changing a number is simply substituting one figure for another.
